questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Exploring nature, culture, and study in a different academic environment

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I really enjoyed my stay in Melbourne while my experience at the university was mixed

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: There was one information meeting that covered the basics and was sufficient

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not require assistance

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: There were very little social activities as part of the orientation

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found housing through the facebook group "Fairy Floss Real Estate". In general, it appears quite feasible to find something when you start searching 4-6 weeks in advance. After many sent messages and video calls I had several offers well before my departure.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Many buildings in Melbourne, particularly in the suburbs, are poorly insulated so bring extra layers to stay warm during the winter.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: On-campus housing and commercial student accommodation close to the uni are extremely overpriced. I ended up paying 220AUD/week staying in a shared flat in Brunswick.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The registration was relatively straightforward and the processing time was relatively long. However, registering for courses was unnecessarily complicated and the availability of coursework non-elective master's classes was much more limited than anticipated. Furthermore, there was very little information available on courses, making it quite a gamble what content would actually be covered in courses.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They have their own web portal. Registration for courses happens through a study plan one must upload based on an excel template

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I had one or two questions and the support through email was quite helpful. However, to get approval for courses beyond the study plan I had to message course coordinators individually and ask whether they could approve my prerequisites. Some of which never responded.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Quite unsuccessful. I had a pretty long back-and-forth to find classes that interest me and ended up being stuck with a class that was completely different from what I expected and didn't really interest me.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Some classes only start after the re-enrollment period. Thus, you can't change them for another class if they don't meet expectations. I'd recommend playing it safe and already have approval for some alternative options

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The quality and difficulty of classes were very mixed.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: All my courses were master's courses. Some requiring more prerequisites than others.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching is much more old-school than what I've experienced at KU. Class sizes are larger and the top

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
COMP90086 - Computer Vision
ECON90080 - Macroeconomics
PPMN90056 - Business and Government
POLS90034 - International Policymaking in Practice

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Computer vision was quite interesting but covered a range of topics beyond machine learning. 
The class on advanced macroeconomics was taught based on a 1998 book. The content felt outdated and the enthusiasm of the professor felt a bit limited but it was still a relevant introduction to advanced macroeconomic modelling with microfoundations.
Business and government was a highly disappointing class. The teacher, Valarie Sands, seemed not very knowledgeable of the topic and lacked the ability to convey knowledge in an interesting way. The content covered was extremely basic. 
International Policymaking was a good class. The content was catering to a broad audience and hence, quite basic but the teachers we're good and enthusiastic.
In general, the content of most classes felt a bit dated.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are many student-led clubs I'd recommend participating in.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Few activities or events but quite a few clubs.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I became part of the rowing club, MUBC, the Weightlifting club, and the Mountaineering club. Especially the later is a great opportunity to explore nature which can otherwise be quite challenging without a car.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I enjoyed my stay in Tasmania. It's great for hiking and rock climbing.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. Aussies are friendly and open.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a club

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: In many of my classes there were many students from overseas. I experienced that there was a language barrier and different cultural expectations around some groupwork in some of my classes.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Melbourne has a lot to offer. There are many cool little cafés and spots all around town to explore.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: I'd recommend finding off-campus housing. It's cheaper to find a sharehouse and it's a great opportunity to stay with some locals in a sharehouse.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Course enrollment is frustrating and you might not get into the courses you would like to - particularly as an interdisciplinary SDS student. Also, some courses are not exactly what they seem like from the syllabus. Make sure to be flexible with your courses and switch courses if you're not happy with the first week of lectures.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I traveled to multiple regattas with the rowing club and became part of a cool little community.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I chose some courses that were quite challenging for me and definitely panicked a little leading up to the finals.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I have had a previous stay abroad in Canada at the University of Toronto and got the impression that the quality of teaching at North American universities is significantly higher than in Australia.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
